program_name: Bachelor in Tourism, Sport and Event Management
teaching_language: Trilingual (Italian / German / English) — and unusually well documented at course level for this programme, which makes the trilingualism verifiable rather than nominal. The brochure states 'Courses will be taught in: Italian, German and English (trilingual)'. The published course-offering list for the programme shows teaching languages distributed roughly evenly across the three languages, with core compulsory subjects genuinely delivered in German and Italian, not only in English: Micro and Macroeconomics (8 CP, 1st year, compulsory) is taught in GERMAN; Tourism and Sport Law (6 CP, 1st year, compulsory) and Managerial Economics for TSE (6 CP, 2nd year, compulsory) are taught in ITALIAN; Marketing (8 CP, 1st year), Introduction to Management (6 CP), Introduction to Tourism, Sport and Event Management (6 CP), Introduction to Finance (8 CP), Introduction to Accounting for TSE (8 CP) and Managerial Accounting (6 CP) are taught in ENGLISH. A snapshot of the course-offering page yielded approximately 7 English, 6 Italian and 4 German courses plus Spanish/French language courses. In addition, year 1 requires TWO of the three 'Foreign Language – Communication and Presentation Skills in Specialized Language' courses (3 CP each) and students may NOT sit those exams in the language of their secondary-school final exam; year 2 adds a further compulsory 6 CP Foreign Language course in Spanish or French. unibz does not publish an official percentage split of teaching hours per language. [uncertain]
campus: Bruneck-Brunico — but this is a MOVING campus and the detail is decision-critical. The 2026/27 brochure states: 'Campus: Bruneck-Brunico, NOI Techpark Bruneck-Brunico' and classes take place both at the Bruneck-Brunico campus and at the NOI Techpark Bruneck-Brunico. However, the same brochure states: 'Students beginning their studies in the 2026/27 academic year at the Bruneck-Brunico Campus will continue their studies at the Bozen-Bolzano Campus starting from the second year, 2027/28.' So a student entering in 2026/27 spends ONLY year 1 in Bruneck-Brunico (Puster Valley, roughly 80 km northeast of Bolzano) and then relocates to the Bozen-Bolzano main campus for years 2 and 3. This is part of a wider wind-down of the Bruneck site: the Master in Tourism Management at Bruneck is suspended for 2026/27. Practical implication: accommodation, cost of living and travel planning differ between year 1 and years 2-3.
degree_class: L-18 (Scienze dell'economia e della gestione aziendale / Economics and Business Administration). CONFIRMED — the task brief flagged this as 'to be verified' and it is now verified from two independent official sources: the 2026/27 brochure 'At a glance' box states 'Bachelor class: L-18', and both 2026/27 ranking-list PDFs are headed 'Ammissione al corso di laurea in L-18 Management del Turismo, dello Sport e degli Eventi' / 'Zulassung zum Bachelor in L-18 Tourismus-, Sport- und Eventmanagement'. The admission PDF also uses L-18 as its own example when explaining the double-enrolment rule ('the two programmes must not belong to the same class, e.g., L-18/L-18').
offered_in_2026_27: Yes — actively offered and fully run in 2026/27, and notably MORE open than most unibz programmes this cycle. All three intake sessions existed for this programme: Early Bird and Late Application both completed with signed ranking lists published (69 EU admitted in Early Bird, 49 EU admitted in Late), and — unlike the Bachelor in Economics and Management, which was listed as 'Application NOT offered' — this programme IS included in the Additional Application Session. As of the verification date (2026-08-29) that additional session is STILL OPEN: applications run 18/08–04/09/2026 (by noon local time), so roughly six days remained at verification time. The additional session is restricted to EU citizens only. Caveat: the campus relocation from Bruneck-Brunico to Bozen-Bolzano from year two (2027/28) means the programme continues but the Bruneck site itself is being wound down.
is_new_programme: No. This is an established programme of the Faculty of Economics and Management, historically the flagship offering of the Bruneck-Brunico campus. Published course syllabi under the degree 'Tourism, Sport and Event Management' exist for the 2024/2025 academic year and earlier, and a 2025/26 edition of both the admission-information PDF and the brochure was published, so the programme has been running for multiple cycles. The exact first intake year is not stated on any official unibz page. [uncertain]
majors_tracks_study_plans: No formal majors, tracks or separate study plans — a single 180 ECTS / 3-year study plan for all students. Specialisation is achieved through six paired either/or compulsory choices that let a student lean towards SPORT or towards TOURISM. Year 1 (fixed core): Introduction to Management 6 CP; Mathematics for Economists TSE 12 CP (two 6 CP modules); Tourism and Sport Law 6 CP; Introduction to Accounting for TSE 8 CP; Micro and Macroeconomics 8 CP; Marketing 8 CP; Introduction to Tourism, Sport and Event Management 6 CP; plus TWO of the three Foreign Language – Communication and Presentation Skills in Specialized Language courses (German / Italian / English, 3 CP each). Year 2: Managerial Economics for TSE 6 CP; Statistics for TSE 6 CP; Managerial Accounting 6 CP; Introduction to Finance 8 CP; Foreign Language (Spanish or French) 6 CP; Entrepreneurship and Leadership 12 CP (M-1 Strategic Management + M-2 Organisational Behaviour and Leadership); Group 1 choice — Economics of Sport and Events OR Economics of Tourism and Destinations; Group 2 choice — Event Management and Planning OR Sport and Facility Management. Year 3: Business Law for TSE 12 CP (M-1 Foundations of Business Law + M-2 Applied Business Law); Soft Skills and Problem Solving Abilities 4 CP; Group 3 choice — Experiential Tourism and Events: Food and Wine OR Sustainable Consumption in Tourism, Sport and Events; Group 4 choice — Sport Marketing and Sponsorship OR Strategic Marketing for Tourism; Group 5 choice — Current Issues in Sport Management OR Current Issues in Tourism Management; Group 6 choice — Quantitative Methods in Management OR Data Management, Analysis and Security; Internship 6 CP; Free Choice 12 CP (may be taken in year 2 or 3); Final Thesis 6 CP. A compulsory internship of at least 150 hours is required. A distinctive feature is the Tourism Management Club (tmc): each year a rotating group of 15 students manages a conference series with speakers from business and academia. Language-course rules: students cannot sit the specialised-language exams in the language of their secondary-school final exam; graduates of a Ladin school in South Tyrol must sit the English exams and choose between German or Italian for the rest; students who graduated in a language other than the three official teaching languages must nominate the two languages in which they will sit the language exams, notifying the Faculty Secretariat.
english_only_accessibility: EFFECTIVELY CLOSED for an English-only candidate — and for this programme the evidence is unusually stark, stronger than for most unibz trilingual degrees. Two independent barriers apply. (1) THE ADMISSION GATE: entry requires B2 in the 1st language AND B2 in the 2nd language across German, Italian and English; a candidate who can certify only English fills at most one position and is excluded from the admission procedure before ranking. This is not theoretical — in the 2026/27 Early Bird round 29 EU applicants were excluded 'for not meeting the language requirements for admission', and in the non-EU-citizens-living-abroad section only TWO applicants appeared and BOTH were excluded on exactly that ground, meaning ZERO non-EU students were admitted to this programme in 2026/27. The Late session excluded a further 10 EU applicants on language grounds. (2) THE CURRICULUM GATE, which is the harder one: even a candidate who somehow cleared admission could not complete year 1 in English, because compulsory first-year courses are taught in German and Italian — Micro and Macroeconomics (8 CP) in German and Tourism and Sport Law (6 CP) in Italian — and year 1 further compels TWO specialised-language courses that cannot be sat in the language of one's own school-leaving exam. Classification: effectively-closed. A Turkish or other international applicant realistically needs a certified B2 in German OR Italian alongside English before this programme becomes reachable at all. Encouraging counter-signal for those who do fix their certification: at least ten Applicant IDs excluded for language in the Early Bird round reappear as ADMITTED in the Late round, so the gate is a certification problem that can be solved between sessions rather than a permanent bar.
admission_type: Restricted access (numero programmato) with competitive ranking — but in practice non-selective for EU applicants in 2026/27 (see selection_scoring). No entrance examination, no TOLC, no SAT, no CENT-S, no interview and no portfolio. Selection is a document- and grade-based dossier evaluation performed by the Admission Committee on the basis of self-declared secondary-school grades plus language-certificate bonus points. Applications are submitted through the unibz Application Portal (https://aws.unibz.it/exup/). Separate quotas and procedures apply to (1) EU citizens and those given parity of treatment and (2) non-EU citizens living abroad. Selection criteria approved by Faculty of Economics Faculty Council Resolution no. 142 of 15.09.2025 — the same resolution that governs the other Faculty of Economics bachelor programmes.
academic_requirements: A secondary school leaving certificate of the Italian system, OR an equivalent qualification obtained abroad. A foreign school leaving certificate counts as equivalent only if it was obtained after 12 years of education AND at least the last two years were attended within that foreign school system (unibz gives the Irish Leaving Certificate as the counter-example: attending only one year and obtaining the certificate is not sufficient). The Italian Ministry of Education, University and Research imposes additional specific requirements on holders of certain qualifications — American high school diplomas, British and Greek certificates are named explicitly — and applicants in those categories are told to contact apply@unibz.it (Advisory Service) before applying. No specific subject prerequisites, no separate minimum GPA gate beyond the 21/33 ranking threshold, and no prior ECTS/SSD requirement (this is a bachelor programme, so the SSD-credit logic that applies to unibz master admissions is not relevant here). Language requirements are a hard admission gate — failing them means exclusion from the procedure before any ranking. Under national rules, simultaneous enrolment in a maximum of two programmes is allowed, provided they are not in the same degree class (explicitly: not L-18 with another L-18) and differ in at least 2/3 of course content — which matters here because the sibling Bachelor in Economics and Management is also L-18 and therefore cannot be combined with this one. Credit points from previous university studies can be recognised only after enrolment, and only where the exams taken at the previous university are equivalent in content to those offered at unibz.
entry_exam_or_test: NO admission entrance exam of any kind — unibz does not use its own subject test, TOLC-I, TOLC-E, CENT-S, SAT or GMAT/GRE for this programme. Admission is purely dossier/ranking based.

Language proficiency exams (optional route, only if you cannot prove your levels by diploma or recognised certificate): organised online by the unibz Language Centre. 2026/27 Early Bird sittings 16/03/2026 (registration 02–09/03/2026) and 16–17 + 20–21/04/2026 (registration 24/03–08/04/2026); Late Application sittings 22–26/06/2026 (registration 28/05–15/06/2026). Registration is done inside the application portal under 'enrol for language exams', and only after an application has been created under 'create/manage applications'. Note: only B2-level exams can be booked, and no Language Centre exam sittings are listed for the Additional Application Session.

Compulsory mathematics test — AFTER admission, not for admission. The faculty runs a preparatory course in mathematics in English before the first semester (2026/27: 21–25/09/2026) and every new student must sit a compulsory test at the end of it. A negative result or non-participation triggers OFA (see ofa_rules).

Third-language placement test — after admission, for students who cannot certify their third language; the result determines the assigned language-learning path aimed at reaching B2 as soon as possible.
selection_scoring: Maximum 33 points, minimum 21/33 required for admission; the final score is rounded up or down. Component (a) — up to 30 points from the grade average of the last two available high-school years (the last two if the final year is already available, otherwise the two years preceding the final year). For each of those years the candidate supplies one mark for each of four subject areas: 1) Language (any, modern or ancient), 2) Mathematics, 3) Humanities and Social Sciences (history, philosophy, politics, sociology, economics, law), 4) Natural and Technical Sciences (physics, chemistry, biology, geography, environmental studies, informatics); plus 2 further marks from areas 1, 3 or 4. If a subject area cannot be filled, a grade from another area may be substituted. Excluded from the calculation: conduct (condotta/Betragen), religion, physical education, performing-arts subjects (instrumental music, singing, drama/theatre) and — notably relevant for this programme's typical applicant pool — subjects closely related to the hospitality sector (cuisine and related areas, restaurant and bar service, oenology). Component (b) — up to 3 language bonus points (see bonus_points). Tie-breakers: higher grade average first, then the younger applicant. If the candidate does not supply grades for a year, the Committee assigns a score corresponding to 'sufficient merit' for that year; for school systems substantially different from the Italian one the Committee may evaluate reports from other years; if the candidate already holds a university degree, the Committee uses the university exam average. ACTUAL 2026/27 OUTCOMES — THIS PROGRAMME WAS UNDERSUBSCRIBED, NOT COMPETITIVE: Early Bird EU admitted only 69 candidates against 80 available places, with NO waiting list at all; top score 32.00, 69th and last admitted 21.02; only 4 applicants were excluded for falling below the minimum (19.76, 19.74, 19.74, 18.99). Late Application EU admitted 49 candidates, again with no waiting list; top score 31.04, 49th and last admitted 20.51 (which rounds to 21); 5 excluded below minimum (20.49, 20.25, 20.01, 19.74, 18.99). Non-EU living abroad: ZERO admitted — only 2 applicants appeared and both were excluded for failing the language requirements. Bottom line for a prospective applicant: essentially every EU candidate who cleared the language gate and reached 21/33 was admitted, and the two sessions together admitted 118 EU students against a published EU quota of 100. The binding constraint on this programme is the LANGUAGE requirement, not the score.
bonus_points: Maximum 3 bonus points, awarded solely for language proficiency ABOVE the level required for admission, on this scale: C1 + C1 + at least B2 = 3 points; C1 + C1 + B1 = 2.5 points; C1 + C1 = 2 points; at least B2 + B2 + B2 = 1 point; at least B2 + B2 + B1 = 0.5 points. Only language certificates recognised by the unibz Language Centre count, as do exams taken at the Language Centre provided a course for the requested level is offered. NO other bonus schemes apply to this programme — there is no Webometrics university-ranking bonus (that is a Master in Software Engineering / Computing for Data Science mechanism), no GMAT/GRE bonus (Master in Accounting and Finance), and no startup-project bonus (Master in Entrepreneurship and Innovation). Given how low the effective cut-off was in 2026/27 (21.02 and 20.51), these bonus points were not decisive for admission in this cycle, though they remain the cheapest way to lift a marginal score.
portfolio_and_materials: None required. No portfolio, no video, no project proposal, no motivation letter, no CV and no reference letters are part of this admission procedure — and therefore no format or file-size limits apply. The only uploads are: a valid identity document, the self-declared grades entered directly in the portal form, scanned copies of school report cards for any self-declared year completed abroad, official translations of those report cards into Italian, German or English where needed, optional language certificates, and the diploma (at application if already held, otherwise at enrolment). Note that one Late-session applicant was excluded specifically 'for not having provided the necessary documents required by the admission procedure', so the minimal document set still has to be complete.
interview: No interview. The admission procedure contains no oral or online interview stage at any point, for either EU or non-EU applicants, and no interview dates are published for this programme.
conditional_admission: Yes, in the bachelor sense: applicants who have not yet completed secondary school may apply and are ranked on the grades of the two years preceding the final year, uploading the diploma at enrolment rather than at application. The ECTS-threshold form of conditional admission (>=120 ECTS, 140 for Data Analytics) does not apply here — that is a unibz master's mechanism. Financial protection: if you pay the first instalment to secure your place but then fail your secondary-school final exam, you ARE entitled to a refund (one of only two refund exceptions; the other is non-EU applicants abroad who cannot obtain the enrolment documents from the Italian authorities in their country). Non-EU citizens living abroad are additionally admitted 'with reservation' (con riserva / mit Vorbehalt) on the ranking list, the reservation being lifted only once the Italian consulate confirms directly to unibz. Missing the fee-payment deadline or the enrolment deadline means automatic exclusion and the next person on the ranking list is admitted. unibz may exclude a student by Rector's decree even after enrolment if the admission qualification turns out not to be valid.
ofa_rules: Yes — OFA (obblighi formativi aggiuntivi / additional learning requirements) applies to this programme, and the field definition in fields.yaml correctly lists Tourism, Sport and Event Management as one of the three programmes concerned. OFA is assigned to any student who fails, or does not attend, the compulsory mathematics test held at the end of the September mathematics preparatory course (2026/27: 21–25/09/2026, taught in English). Three alternative ways to clear it: (1) pass the test offered at the end of the OFA exercise sessions, (2) pass the exam at the end of teaching module 1 of the 'Mathematics' course, or (3) pass the full mathematics exam (teaching module 1 + teaching module 2) within the first academic year. Consequence of not clearing OFA: the student is blocked from sitting the quantitative examinations of years 2 and 3 — for THIS programme specifically those are 'Statistics for TSE', 'Quantitative Methods in Management' and 'Data Management, Analysis and Security' (note this list differs from the Economics and Management list, which names Statistics, Financial Mathematics and the two Econometrics courses).
language_requirements: The official teaching languages are German, Italian and English, and the language requirement is a hard exclusion gate — failing it means exclusion from the admission procedure entirely, not merely a lower score. Requirements are defined by POSITION (1st/2nd/3rd language), not by which specific language: your first language is the one you are strongest in (B2 or C1), your third is the one you are weakest in or an absolute beginner in. Entry: B2 in the 1st language, B2 in the 2nd language, no level required in the 3rd. Exit (to graduate): C1 / C1 / B2, per the Common European Framework of Reference. Certification is MANDATORY for the 1st and 2nd language and only recommended (from B1 upwards) for the 3rd. B1 in the third language is the minimum to sit curricular exams in that language, and if the first semester is taught only in English while English is your third language, you must certify at least B1 in English by mid-January to take all first-semester exams. Free Language Centre courses target B1 in the third language by the end of year 1 and B2 by the end of year 2; three-week intensive courses run in September (2026/27: 01–18/09/2026, Monday to Friday, 6 h/day) and A1 beginner courses are now offered ONLY in that September window and no longer during the academic year, so absolute beginners must start there. Extensive courses (4 h/week) run during semesters, intensive courses (6 h/day) between semesters; all Language Centre courses are free of charge. Higher-than-required levels earn up to 3 ranking bonus points. For this programme the language gate is the single most consequential requirement: it accounted for 29 EU exclusions in Early Bird, 10 in Late, and both of the only two non-EU applicants.
entry_levels_by_position: 1st language: B2 — 2nd language: B2 — 3rd language: no level required at entry. (Pattern B2/B2/none.) The positions are self-assigned by proficiency across German, Italian and English, so any two of the three languages may fill positions 1 and 2. Conditional follow-on requirements: B1 in the 3rd language is required to sit curricular examinations in that language, and B1 in English by mid-January if English is your 3rd language and your first semester is English-only. Note that only B2-level exams can be booked at the unibz Language Centre, so a candidate who needs to prove C1 (for bonus points) must bring an external recognised certificate rather than sitting a Language Centre exam.
exit_levels: 1st language: C1 — 2nd language: C1 — 3rd language: B2. CEFR levels. This is the standard unibz trilingual exit pattern and it is a graduation condition, not a recommendation: a student admitted with B2/B2/none must raise two languages to C1 and reach B2 in the third before graduating. The Language Centre's free course path is calibrated to this trajectory (B1 in the third language by end of year 1, B2 by end of year 2). The curriculum reinforces it structurally — year 1 forces two specialised-language courses in languages other than the one used for the school-leaving exam, and year 2 adds a further 6 CP foreign language (Spanish or French) on top of the three official languages.
third_language_exam_threshold: B1 in the third language is the minimum for taking curricular examinations in that specific language. Special case flagged by unibz: if the first semester of the programme is taught only in English and English is your third language, you must certify at least B1 in English by mid-January in order to sit all the curricular exams scheduled for the first semester. Students who cannot certify the third language on admission take a placement test after admission (details sent by e-mail) and are assigned a learning path aimed at reaching B2 as quickly as possible. Practical note for this programme: because compulsory first-year courses are actually delivered in German (Micro and Macroeconomics) and Italian (Tourism and Sport Law), the B1 third-language threshold bites early and is not a formality that can be deferred.
proof_pathways: Four accepted routes, all handled inside the application portal (sections 'upload language certificates' and 'enrol for language exams', which become available only after creating an application under 'create/manage applications'). (1) The main teaching language of your FINAL high-school year, if German, Italian or English — recognised as C1. Ladin upper-secondary schools are recognised as B2 in German and Italian. For foreign qualifications, if the medium of instruction is not clearly stated on the diploma you must also upload a letter or document from the school stating it. (2) A bachelor or master degree taught in Italian, German or English — recognised as C1; the same medium-of-instruction letter rule applies to foreign degrees; unibz graduates upload their Language Centre certificates or declare the B2/B2+/C1 exams they passed. (3) A recognised language certificate from the official unibz list (https://www.unibz.it/assets/Documents/Languages/unibz-recognised-language-certificates-v2.pdf); if it cannot be uploaded it may be e-mailed as a PDF or delivered in person to the Language Centre by the application deadline. (4) A language exam organised by the unibz Language Centre — 2026/27 online sittings: 16/03/2026 (registration 02–09/03/2026) and 16–17 + 20–21/04/2026 (registration 24/03–08/04/2026) for Early Bird, and 22–26/06/2026 (registration 28/05–15/06/2026) for Late Application; only B2-level exams can be booked, and if you start your application outside a registration window you must return to the portal during one of the windows to register. A fifth partial route exists for bi-/multilingual and foreign schools: if the diploma explicitly states CEFR levels (B1/B2/C1) for German, Italian or English AND all four language abilities (reading, listening, speaking, writing) were assessed, those levels are accepted as proof for the 2nd and/or 3rd language — upload the school leaving certificate under the respective language and the Language Centre decides on recognition. Formalities: a certificate awarded by an Italian public institution is submitted as a self-declaration; one awarded by a foreign public institution requires an uploaded scanned copy of the original.
certificate_rules: Governed by Resolution of the University Council no. 16/2026 (Beschluss des Universitätsrates / Delibera del Consiglio dell'Università n. 16/2026), verified directly from the recognised-certificates document. Core rules: (1) the certificate must include the assessment of ALL FOUR skills and be issued by the certification organisation itself; (2) it must indicate adequate performance in all skills as an overall grade, or the detailed assessment must appear on the certificate itself or in appropriate documentation faithful to the original from the issuer; (3) if no overall result and/or level is stated, the LOWEST level reached in any subskill is decisive, provided that part of the examination was passed; (4) there is no compensation for 'failed' parts and no averages are calculated unless the certification organisation itself provides for it; (5) certificates issued by exam boards and obtained by taking an online exam ('home edition') are NOT recognised, except for those explicitly indicated in the list; (6) certificates regarding single skills issued by different certification organisations are not accepted; (7) certificates of participation, end-of-course tests and examinations from private educational institutions, and placement-test results are not recognised; (8) certificates issued by individual lecturers or teaching staff are not recognised; (9) DAAD certificates are explicitly NOT recognised. Validity: international language certificates must not be older than five years before the date of submission, with the entire calendar year applying from 1 January (i.e. a certificate issued from 1 January of the fifth year preceding submission remains valid throughout that year). Items listed under 'Further Recognised Degrees, Diplomas and Certificates' have unlimited validity.
application_deadline_eu: THREE sessions were open for EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment in 2026/27 — this programme, unlike the Bachelor in Economics and Management, did receive an Additional Application Session. (1) EARLY BIRD — application 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28, by noon local time (unibz notation 02/03 - 28/04/2026). (2) LATE APPLICATION (EU citizens only) — application 2026-05-28 to 2026-07-08, by noon local time (28/05 - 08/07/2026). (3) ADDITIONAL APPLICATION SESSION (EU citizens only) — application 2026-08-18 to 2026-09-04, by noon local time (18/08 - 04/09/2026). AS OF THE VERIFICATION DATE 2026-08-29 THE ADDITIONAL SESSION IS STILL OPEN, with the deadline six days away; the unibz additional-application-session page lists this programme as 'Application possible'. Applicants excluded in an earlier session may re-apply in a later one, and EU applicants may apply to more than one study programme — the 2026/27 ranking lists show at least ten Applicant IDs that were excluded on language grounds in Early Bird and then admitted in the Late session after fixing their certification.
application_deadline_non_eu: ONE window only: 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28, by noon local time (Early Bird, unibz notation 02/03 - 28/04/2026). Non-EU citizens living outside Italy have no Late Application and no Additional Session — 'Only one application period is offered. After the deadline it is not possible to apply anymore.' A non-refundable EUR 50 application fee applies. Downstream 2026/27 dates matched Early Bird: ranking by 2026-05-27, first instalment by 2026-06-05 (noon), enrolment 2026-07-10 to 2026-08-06 (noon). Universitaly pre-enrolment is mandatory after paying the first instalment, and admission on the ranking list is granted 'with reservation' until the Italian consulate confirms directly to unibz. HARD REALITY CHECK for 2026/27: this single window produced only two non-EU applicants and both were excluded for failing the language requirements, so no non-EU student was admitted to this programme at all. For a non-EU applicant targeting 2027/28, the window will fall around early March to late April 2027 and the binding preparation task is certifying B2 in a second language (German or Italian) well before it opens.
parity_of_treatment: Two categories are treated as EU-equivalent and therefore gain access to the Late Application and Additional sessions and the much larger EU quota. (1) Citizens of Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Switzerland, San Marino and Vatican City State. (2) Non-EU citizens holding a valid Italian permit to stay (permesso di soggiorno) under article 39 paragraph 5 of Decree no. 286 of 25.07.1998 — issued for WORK, FAMILY reasons, political or humanitarian ASYLUM, or RELIGIOUS reasons. They apply directly to the University and must submit a copy of the valid permit; if it has expired, a renewal request must be attached. CRITICAL FOR TURKISH AND OTHER NON-EU APPLICANTS: a permit to stay for STUDY reasons and a tourism visa are explicitly NOT sufficient. If the permit is not uploaded in the application portal, the applicant is automatically reclassified as a non-EU citizen living abroad and pushed into the Italian-consulate procedure with the far smaller quota (4 places versus 100) and a single application window. For this programme the stakes of that reclassification are unusually high, because the EU/equivalent route was effectively non-competitive in 2026/27 while the non-EU route admitted nobody.
places_quotas: Three separate numbers for 2026/27, total 104. EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment: 80 in Early Bird + 20 in Late Application = 100. Non-EU citizens living abroad: 4, Early Bird only. Any places left unfilled by EU/equivalent candidates in the Early Bird round roll over into the Late Application round for EU/equivalent candidates. WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED IN 2026/27: Early Bird admitted only 69 EU/equivalent candidates against 80 places, leaving 11 unfilled and producing NO waiting list; the Late session then admitted 49 EU candidates, also with no waiting list; and the programme still went to an Additional Application Session in August–September. Note the arithmetic anomaly — 69 + 49 = 118 EU admissions against a published EU quota of 100, so the quota was evidently not binding in practice and unibz admitted every EU applicant who cleared the language gate and reached the 21/33 threshold. The non-EU quota of 4 went entirely unused: only 2 non-EU applicants applied and both were excluded on language grounds. The additional-session page does not publish a place count for this programme. [uncertain — the 118-versus-100 discrepancy is an observed fact from the signed ranking lists but unibz publishes no explanation for it; the likely mechanisms are rollover of unpaid Early Bird places plus faculty discretion, neither of which is documented]
ranking_and_enrolment_dates: EARLY BIRD 2026/27 — ranking lists published by 2026-05-27; first instalment of tuition fees (the payment that actually secures the place) by 2026-06-05 noon local time; enrolment window 2026-07-10 to 2026-08-06 noon. LATE APPLICATION 2026/27 — ranking lists published by 2026-07-30; first instalment by 2026-08-06 noon; enrolment from publication of the ranking list until 2026-08-06 noon. ADDITIONAL APPLICATION SESSION 2026/27 — ranking lists published by 2026-09-18; first instalment by 2026-09-25 noon; enrolment from publication of the ranking list until 2026-09-25 noon (this round was still pending as of the 2026-08-29 verification date). Missing the payment deadline means automatic exclusion and the next candidate on the list is admitted; missing the enrolment deadline has the same effect. A candidate admitted to more than one programme may secure a maximum of two places by paying the designated rate twice. Paying does NOT confer student status — only enrolment does — and there is no refund if you pay but do not enrol, except if you fail your secondary-school final exam or (non-EU abroad) cannot obtain the enrolment documents from the Italian authorities. unibz recommends enrolling as early as possible so that incomplete documents can still be corrected before the deadline. Ranking lists are valid for the respective academic year only. Once enrolled, the faculty fee calendar differs from the admission calendar: first instalment due 13/10/2026 and second by 31/03/2027 per the Faculty of Economics fee page.
programme_specific_dates: 2026/27 calendar from the programme's own admission-information PDF. Language exams (online): 16/03/2026 (registration 02–09/03/2026); 16–17 and 20–21/04/2026 (registration 24/03–08/04/2026); 22–26/06/2026 (registration 28/05–15/06/2026). Intensive language courses: 01–18/09/2026, Monday to Friday, 6 h/day. Mathematics pre-courses: 21/09/2026–25/09/2026, followed immediately by the compulsory mathematics test that determines OFA. required_documents: AT APPLICATION (uploaded in the unibz Application Portal, https://aws.unibz.it/exup/): (1) a valid ID card or passport, front and back — an invalid, incomplete or unreadable document means exclusion from the admission procedure; (2) the completed online application form, including the self-declaration of grades for the four subject areas plus two extra subjects for each of the two relevant high-school years (secondary schools in Germany: insert the 'Jahreszeugnis' grades, or if unavailable the average of the two 'Halbjahreszeugnisse' with decimal place); (3) a copy of the relevant school report cards for any self-declared year completed abroad; (4) official translation of the school report cards into Italian, German or English where needed; (5) optionally, language certificates for the entry-level proof and the bonus-point calculation; (6) the diploma of the qualification if already obtained, otherwise at enrolment. Mendacious declarations are criminally prosecuted and cause automatic exclusion from the ranking list. Once sent, the application cannot be modified, and forms that are filled in but not correctly submitted are disregarded — one Late-session applicant was excluded in 2026/27 precisely for not providing the required documents. AT ENROLMENT, for a foreign secondary-school qualification: the secondary school diploma; an official translation of the diploma into Italian (not required for diplomas issued in German or English); plus the ARDI/CIMEA statements described under credential_recognition. NOTE: the structured 'study career' Excel template that unibz requires for master's applications is NOT part of this bachelor procedure. Transfer students from another Italian university must additionally submit a copy of the transfer application filed at their previous university to the Student Office at the start of the academic year. unibz may request further documents in case of doubt and can exclude a student by Rector's decree even after enrolment if the admission qualification is not valid.
application_fee: EUR 50, payable ONLY by non-EU citizens living abroad. It is an administration fee and is explicitly non-refundable. EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment pay no application fee.
tuition_or_fees_link: https://guide.unibz.it/en/study-career/economics-management/fees — EUR 1,200 per year for students within the normal programme length, split into two instalments of EUR 600. The 1st instalment includes the EUR 16 revenue stamp (marca da bollo) and, during the admission procedure, is the payment that secures the admitted place (2026/27 admission deadlines: 05/06/2026 Early Bird, 06/08/2026 Late, 25/09/2026 Additional). Once enrolled, the faculty fee calendar is 1st instalment by 13/10/2026 and 2nd instalment by 31/03/2027 (the admission PDF states more generally 'by March of the following year'). Students beyond the normal programme length (fuori corso) pay EUR 1,500 (EUR 900 + EUR 600). Late payment of the second instalment incurs a EUR 30 fine and blocks the online account, exam registration and transfers to other universities or programmes. No refund on drop-out, interruption or exclusion. Full exemption (paying only the EUR 16 stamp) applies to students with a disability recognised under art. 3 para. 1 of Law 104/1992 or a disability of 66% or more — the health-authority certificate must be handed in at the start of the academic year — and to foreign students holding an Italian government scholarship. Freemover students studying abroad for both semesters pay nothing; for the first semester only, the 2nd instalment is still due by 31/03. Students concluding their studies by 31 October owe no annual fee; by 31 March, only the EUR 16 stamp duty. Holders of a scholarship from the Autonomous Province of Bozen-Bolzano receive a refund of the tuition fees, usually in March–April, though the refund does not cover late-payment fines.
scholarships_grants: (1) Provincial study grant from the Autonomous Province of Bozen-Bolzano, applied for via the Office for the Right to Study (Ufficio per il diritto allo studio universitario) through its e-government online service; the office administers three annual categories — ordinary study grants, merit scholarships and postgraduate support. Holders also get their unibz tuition fees refunded. Indicative amounts of approximately EUR 1,680 to EUR 6,960 per year depending on income are cited in unibz materials, but the current Study Grants page does not restate them. [uncertain — amount range not confirmed on the live 2026/27 page]. CRITICAL RESTRICTION FOR NON-EU APPLICANTS, quoted from the unibz Study Guide: non-EU students can apply for a study grant only if they hold a long-term residence permit or after having been resident in South Tyrol for at least one uninterrupted year — so a first-year non-EU student arriving on a study visa is effectively excluded from it in year 1. (2) Merit-based scholarships exist from the second year onwards; the live page references them without publishing a grade threshold (a 27/30 exam average is the figure commonly cited in unibz materials). [uncertain — threshold not confirmed on the live page]. (3) Tuition-fee exemption for Italian-government scholarship holders and for students with a recognised disability (see tuition_or_fees_link). (4) The page also lists scholarships from Italian banks, German and Austrian funding programmes, and municipality-specific awards. (5) The student associations sh.asus and MUA assist with the grant application. No programme-specific scholarship is advertised for the Bachelor in Tourism, Sport and Event Management on its own page. Contact: study@unibz.it, +39 0471 012900. Source: https://guide.unibz.it/en/life-on-campus/study-grants
credential_recognition: Required at ENROLMENT for holders of a foreign secondary-school qualification, in three tiers set out verbatim in the admission PDF. (a) EU countries, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, International Baccalaureate, European Baccalaureate: Statement of Correspondence of the secondary school diploma, downloaded from ARDI (Automatic Recognition Database – Italy). (b) Non-EU countries that are signatories to the Lisbon Convention: Statement of Correspondence from ARDI PLUS Statement of Verification issued by CIMEA (Italian Information Centre on Academic Mobility and Equivalence). (c) Non-EU countries that are NOT signatories of the Lisbon Convention: Statement of Comparability issued by CIMEA PLUS Statement of Verification issued by CIMEA. In all cases the diploma itself and an official Italian translation must be uploaded — the translation is not needed for diplomas issued in German or English. The 12-years-of-education rule and the last-two-years-in-that-school-system rule (see academic_requirements) apply in parallel. unibz performs its own checks and reserves the right to request additional documents; an invalid admission qualification can lead to exclusion by Rector's decree even after enrolment. The 180-ECTS Diploma Supplement evidence mentioned in the field definition applies to master's admissions, not to this bachelor. Turkey is a Lisbon Convention signatory, so Turkish applicants fall under tier (b): ARDI Statement of Correspondence plus CIMEA Statement of Verification. [uncertain — the tier assignment for Turkey is inferred from Turkey's Lisbon Convention membership; unibz publishes the rule by tier, not by country, so Turkish applicants should confirm with apply@unibz.it]
non_eu_visa_process: Sequence for non-EU citizens living abroad: apply in the single Early Bird window with the EUR 50 non-refundable fee -> ranking list published (admission granted 'with reservation') -> pay the 1st instalment to secure the place -> start the visa application on the Universitaly portal, which is MANDATORY (without it you will not be allowed to enrol) and on which you may select ONE study programme only -> the Italian authorities in your country issue the entry visa for studies/university, which allows you to enrol for the programme you applied for -> enrol at unibz. Within 8 working days of arrival in Italy you must have applied for the residence permit (permesso di soggiorno) — contact the Advisory Service immediately on arrival for the procedure — and once obtained, the permit must be handed in at the Student Office in person or by e-mail. Refund exception: non-EU applicants abroad who pay but cannot obtain the necessary enrolment documents from the Italian authorities in their country are entitled to a refund. Proof of means of subsistence for the visa (roughly EUR 800 per month, total of at least EUR 36,000 for a bachelor programme) and the 20 hours per week / 1,040 hours per year work cap are general Italian and unibz rules rather than items restated in this programme's admission PDF. [uncertain — the specific subsistence and work-hour figures are not printed in this programme's admission-information PDF and were carried over from unibz's general international-student guidance]. Programme-specific warning: for 2026/27 the non-EU route to this degree produced zero admissions, both applicants having failed the language gate long before the visa stage became relevant.

uncertainty_notes: 1) CYCLE STATUS — all data is the 2026/27 cycle. Unlike most unibz programmes, this one is NOT fully closed as of the verification date (2026-08-29): the Early Bird and Late sessions are finished with signed ranking lists, but the Additional Application Session (18/08–04/09/2026, EU citizens only) is still open with about six days remaining, and its ranking list is due by 18/09/2026. The 2027/28 call, quotas and dates are not yet published. 2) Both official PDFs carry 'Latest update: 24.08.2026' and are explicitly marked 'Subject to change'. 3) TEACHING-LANGUAGE WEIGHTING — unibz publishes no percentage split of teaching hours per language. The distribution given in teaching_language was reconstructed from the public course-offering page and individual syllabi; the syllabus evidence cited (Marketing = English, Managerial Economics for TSE = Italian) is from the 2024/2025 academic year, and course-level teaching languages can be reassigned between years. The trilingual classification itself is certain; only the weighting is uncertain. 4) QUOTA ARITHMETIC — the two completed sessions admitted 118 EU candidates against a published EU quota of 100 (80 + 20). This is read directly from the signed ranking lists and is not a transcription error, but unibz publishes no explanation for exceeding the quota; the plausible mechanisms (rollover of places from admitted candidates who did not pay, plus faculty discretion in an undersubscribed programme) are inferred, not documented. 5) ADDITIONAL SESSION PLACES — the additional-application-session page confirms 'Application possible' for this programme but does not publish a number of available places. 6) FIRST INTAKE YEAR is not published; the 'not a new programme' assessment rests on 2024/2025 syllabi and a 2025/26 edition of the official PDFs. 7) OFFICIAL CALL — there is no standalone English call/manifesto PDF; Faculty Council Resolution 142 of 15.09.2025 is cited in the ranking lists but is not downloadable, so official_call_url is a best-effort answer. 8) SCHOLARSHIPS — the live unibz Study Grants page confirms the categories and the non-EU residence restriction but does not restate the EUR 1,680–6,960 range or the 27/30 merit threshold, so those two figures are carried from prior unibz materials and may be out of date. 9) NON-EU VISA FIGURES — the EUR 800/month subsistence, EUR 36,000 bachelor total and 20 h/week work cap are general unibz/Italian rules and do not appear in this programme's own admission PDF. 10) TURKEY'S CREDENTIAL TIER (ARDI Statement of Correspondence + CIMEA Statement of Verification) is inferred from Turkey's Lisbon Convention membership, since unibz publishes the rule by tier rather than by country. 11) The ranking-list PDFs are published only in Italian and German; the English admission PDF does not report cut-off scores, so every cut-off figure here was read from the bilingual IT/DE documents. 12) CAMPUS — the Bruneck-to-Bolzano relocation from year two is stated in the official 2026/27 brochure and is therefore certain; the accompanying report that the Bruneck master's programme is suspended for 2026/27 comes from secondary reporting rather than a unibz page and is contextual only. 13) The 'effectively-closed' verdict for English-only candidates is an interpretation, but it rests on two hard facts rather than one: the B2/B2 position rule combined with 41 documented language exclusions across the two 2026/27 sessions (29 + 10 EU and 2 non-EU), and compulsory first-year courses that are actually delivered in German and Italian.
